long_biography.plain_text:
Van Nieuwland began as a freelance programmer while studying informatics at Delft University of Technology. In 1984 he joined five colleagues to create the accounting-software business that became Exact. He worked across programming, new products, e-business and commercial leadership as the company expanded internationally and listed in Amsterdam.

After leaving operations at Exact, he co-founded Yuki to automate cloud accounting for entrepreneurs and accountancy firms. Visma acquired Yuki from Van Nieuwland and Lucas Brentjens in 2020. He and Brentjens also built CNBB Equity Partners, where he now serves as managing partner, investing in and supporting growth and buyout strategies for business-to-business software companies.

uncertainties.detail: The exact rare name, Dutch geography and connected Exact-Yuki-CNBB career make the public identity collision-resistant. A public racing record provides a direct context bridge, but its private-vessel facts are excluded from biographies, classifications, tags and proposals.

Van Nieuwland's fortune was built in Technology, but his current official role is managing partner of a growth and buyout investor. Finance & Investments and Investor therefore describe the present relationship, while the biographies preserve his historically defining software-founder identity.

Sources establish a freelance programmer and student who co-founded the core company, retained substantial founder equity and later created a second platform. They do not document family circumstances or starting support well enough to distinguish independent-start from advantaged-start, so broad Self-made is used.

Van Nieuwland left day-to-day operations in 2005 while retaining shares. Public sources do not provide a complete disposal schedule for his Exact stake, so the dossier does not claim that the later Apax acquisition was his direct exit or assign its full value to him.

Independent reporting identifies Van Nieuwland and Brentjens as selling owners when Visma acquired Yuki, but no price or individual split was disclosed. The transaction establishes a material founder exit without supporting a personal proceeds estimate.

The authoritative source already records 1963. A registry aggregator points to July 1963 for an exact-name French company manager, but no reviewed primary record conclusively bridges that month to this owner, so no day, month, place or birth-country proposal is made.

The exact LinkedIn profile is verified through CNBB, software-investment content and Netherlands geography. No personal Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal domain supplied enough collision-resistant public anchors; the official CNBB domain is proposed only as Company Website.

Enterprise software captures the two historically defining founder platforms, and Private equity captures the current CNBB mandate. Venture capital is omitted because CNBB's current growth and buyout strategy is more precisely represented by Private equity, avoiding overlapping investment tags.

The short biography is 51 words, and the independent long profile is 103 words across two paragraphs with only two explicit years. Both exclude private-vessel facts, volatile portfolio valuations and source narration.
